1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 1

Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence. Article 2

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights. Paragraph (3)

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings; to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Paragraph (4)

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and group.

Paragraph (5)

The best interests of victims are all actions concerning victims undertaken by the Government, Community, Legislative Body, Judicial Body, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 3

The Objectives of Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence are to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of children occurring in households and or public.

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance, whether medically, psychologically or legally, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the Promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of West Manggarai Regency.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST MANGGARAI REGENCY NUMBER 1 YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE.

REGENT OF WEST MANGGARAI

EAST NUSA TENGGARA PROVINCE

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST MANGGARAI REGENCY NUMBER 1 OF 2017

CONCERNING

SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF WEST MANGGARAI,

Considering : a. b. c. that violence and discrimination in any form against women and children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore violence and discrimination against women and children occurring in West Manggarai Regency must receive optimal services and protection; that the provision of services for women victims of violence and child protection is one of the authorities of the regency government in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, thus it needs to be regulated by Regional Regulation; that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence;

In View of : 1. 2.

3.

Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;

Law Number 8 of 2003 concerning the Establishment of West Manggarai Regency in East Nusa Tenggara Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 28, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4271);

Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587); As has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 09 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5070);

With Mutual Approval of

OF WEST MANGGARAI REGENCY

THE REGENT OF WEST MANGGARAI

HAS DECIDED :

To Enact : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 12

(1) Funds for organizing services and protection for women and children victims of violence are sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD) of the Regency.

(2) funds as referred to in paragraph (1) may also come from other legal sources.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

Obtaining information about the existence of complaint centers, Women and Children Service Centers (P3A) and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

What is meant by "Integrated Services" is services that include medical, medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by "Continuous Handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological recovery, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 7

(1) The Regent establishes a community service work unit that functions as a facilitator for P3A.

(2) P3A as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may conduct partnerships with social community institutions and customary functionaries engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.

(3) Further provisions regarding P3A institutions are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 5

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling either from individuals, groups or institutions whether Government or Non-Government.

Article 9

Services and Protection for victims are conducted free of charge, quickly, safely, empathetically, non-discriminatorily, easily accessible and with guaranteed confidentiality.

Article 3

What is meant by "gender-based violence" is action based on gender relations that places women subordinate to men.

CHAPTER IV

VICTIMS' RIGHTS

Article 11

Accompaniment is carried out by persons or bodies/institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

CONCERNING

SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

Obtaining information about the existence of complaint centers, Women and Children Service Centers (P3A) and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

What is meant by "Integrated Services" is services that include medical, medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by "Continuous Handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological recovery, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 3

What is meant by "gender-based violence" is action based on gender relations that places women subordinate to men.

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance, whether medically, psychologically or legally, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.

10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The Objectives of Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence are to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of children occurring in households and or public.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance, whether medically, psychologically or legally, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 12

(1) Funds for organizing services and protection for women and children victims of violence are sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD) of the Regency.

(2) funds as referred to in paragraph (1) may also come from other legal sources.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 11

Accompaniment is carried out by persons or bodies/institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Paragraph (4)

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and group.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.

6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Part Two

Forms and Mechanisms of Services and Protection

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 7

(1) The Regent establishes a community service work unit that functions as a facilitator for P3A.

(2) P3A as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may conduct partnerships with social community institutions and customary functionaries engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.

(3) Further provisions regarding P3A institutions are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The Objectives of Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence are to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of children occurring in households and or public.

Part Three

Principles of Services and Protection

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance, whether medically, psychologically or legally, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF WEST MANGGARAI,

Considering : a. b. c. that violence and discrimination in any form against women and children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore violence and discrimination against women and children occurring in West Manggarai Regency must receive optimal services and protection; that the provision of services for women victims of violence and child protection is one of the authorities of the regency government in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, thus it needs to be regulated by Regional Regulation; that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence;

In View of : 1. 2.

3.

Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;

Law Number 8 of 2003 concerning the Establishment of West Manggarai Regency in East Nusa Tenggara Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 28, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4271);

Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587); As has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 09 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5070);

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by :

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims in providing counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution that provides services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins, etc.) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 7

(1) The Regent establishes a community service work unit that functions as a facilitator for P3A.

(2) P3A as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may conduct partnerships with social community institutions and customary functionaries engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.

(3) Further provisions regarding P3A institutions are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 5

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling either from individuals, groups or institutions whether Government or Non-Government.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously, sustainably, systematically pursued and guarantee the physical, mental, spiritual and social growth and development of children so as to realize a good life and become potential, resilient successors to the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also ensures that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially

the Government and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 states that women as the Mother of the nation and children as the nation's future generation are creatures created by Almighty God and must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect preserved in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and group.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking legal, political, economic and social actions to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.
